title: Messiah
definition: Messiah means Anointed One and refers to Jesus as the promised Christ sent by God to save, rule, shepherd, and restore His people.
summary: Jesus is the promised Messiah who fulfills God's saving promises.
christFocus: As Messiah, Jesus fulfills the Law, Prophets, Psalms, promises, and hopes of God's people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The title Messiah means Anointed One. In the Old Testament, kings, priests, and prophets were anointed for service. Jesus fulfills and surpasses these offices.

He is not merely one deliverer among many; He is the promised Christ who brings salvation, announces the kingdom, bears sin, rises from the dead, and reigns as Lord.

The messianic identity of Jesus shows the unity of Scripture and the faithfulness of God to His promises.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People may admire Jesus while missing His promised role as Christ. This doctrine matters because Jesus must be received as the Messiah God sent, not remade into a human preference.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Read Scripture with expectation that God's promises find fulfillment in Christ. Worship Jesus as Messiah and proclaim Him as the hope of sinners.

relatedTopics: Resurrection, Ascension, and Return of Christ
